title: Bowflex E1 - Speed Sensor Error
shortDescription: Treadmill speed sensor is not reporting to the console.
fullDescription:
Bowflex treadmills such as the Treadmill 10 and BXT series use a reed-switch style speed sensor at the front roller. E1 appears when the sensor cannot detect the magnet rotating past. Usually the sensor has shifted out of range or its wire is loose.

Realign or replace the sensor to clear.

fixSteps.title: Remove hood
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and remove motor hood cover.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor gap
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust sensor bracket so the sensor is 2-3mm from the magnet.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Replace hood and test at 1 mph.

whenToCallPro: Call if sensor is in spec but E1 persists.

faq.a: No - match the Bowflex part number for your model.

title: Bowflex E2 - Incline Motor Error
shortDescription: Incline motor is not responding to calibration.
fullDescription: E2 signals the incline cannot home or move through its range. Start by running the treadmill's incline calibration sequence. If that fails, the lift motor or position sensor is likely faulty.

fixSteps.title: Calibrate incline
fixSteps.instruction: Consult owner's manual for incline calibration key sequence.

fixSteps.title: Inspect lift assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and look for bent tube or loose wiring under the deck.

whenToCallPro: Call if calibration fails and lift motor swap is beyond your comfort.

faq.a: Yes, usually 2-year parts on Bowflex treadmills.

title: Bowflex E3 - Overheat Protection
shortDescription: Motor or controller reached thermal limit.
fullDescription: E3 on Bowflex treadmills means the controller has shut down to prevent heat damage. Lubricate the belt, allow an hour to cool, and ensure adequate ventilation around the motor area.
whenToCallPro: If E3 returns within hours after lubrication, the motor is weak.

title: Bowflex E4 - Console Communication Error
shortDescription: Console lost communication with motor controller.
fullDescription: E4 usually indicates a loose data cable between the console and the motor controller. Reseat both ends of the cable running up through the upright.

fixSteps.title: Reseat upper
fixSteps.instruction: Open console back and reseat data connector.

fixSteps.title: Reseat lower
fixSteps.instruction: Open motor hood and reseat data connector at motor board.

whenToCallPro: Call if cable tests good but E4 persists.

faq.a: No - the treadmill will not start.

title: Bowflex E5 - Over-current Fault
shortDescription: Motor controller detected excessive current draw.
fullDescription: E5 indicates the drive motor is pulling too much current. This is often caused by a jammed belt, a seized roller, or a failing motor. Stop using and inspect for mechanical binding.

fixSteps.title: Inspect belt
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, manually rotate belt - should turn freely.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate
fixSteps.instruction: If belt is dry, lubricate and retest.

whenToCallPro: Call if belt rotates freely but E5 persists - likely motor or controller.

faq.a: It can be - stop use until resolved to prevent electrical damage.

title: Bowflex E6 - Safety Key Error
shortDescription: Safety key not detected by console.
fullDescription: The magnetic safety key was removed, lost, or is not seating correctly. Treadmill will not operate without a properly seated key.

fixSteps.title: Order replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If key is lost, order a Bowflex-branded replacement.

title: Bowflex E7 - Speed Mismatch
shortDescription: Console commanded speed differs from actual speed significantly.
fullDescription: E7 is thrown when the speed feedback differs from the target by too much for too long. Common causes are a slipping walking belt or a worn drive belt under the hood.

fixSteps.title: Tighten belt
fixSteps.instruction: 1/4 turn each rear roller bolt clockwise.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drive belt
fixSteps.instruction: Remove hood and inspect drive belt for glaze or cracks.

whenToCallPro: Call if belts are fine but E7 continues.

title: Bowflex Heart Rate Monitor Not Working
shortDescription: Grip or chest HRM not reporting heart rate.
fullDescription: Bowflex treadmills support grip-sensors on the handlebars and Bluetooth chest straps. Dry hands or a dead strap battery are the most common causes of no reading.

fixSteps.title: Moisten hands
fixSteps.instruction: Dampen palms before gripping the HR pads.

faq.a: Yes, chest straps are more accurate than grip sensors.

title: Bowflex Console No Power
fullDescription: No power to the console usually means a tripped breaker on the treadmill, unplugged cord, or blown fuse on the motor control board.

fixSteps.title: Check breaker
fixSteps.instruction: Flip the breaker on the treadmill frame.

whenToCallPro: Call if breaker and outlet are fine but no power to console.

faq.a: Do NOT use a surge protector - plug directly into wall.

title: Bowflex Walking Belt Slips Under Foot
shortDescription: Belt hesitates or slips when user steps on it.
fullDescription: Slipping belts are caused by under-tensioned walking belts or dry decks with high friction. Properly tensioning and lubricating usually eliminates slip.

fixSteps.title: Tighten belt
fixSteps.instruction: 1/4 turn each rear roller bolt clockwise.

fixSteps.title: Lubricate deck
fixSteps.instruction: Apply silicone lube under belt centerline.

whenToCallPro: If slip continues after tensioning, roller or motor may be worn.

faq.a: Yes - too tight causes roller bearing wear and high motor load.
